name: agentic-challenges
title: Hard agentic-modeling challenges
lead: A benchmark suite: each task is a real composite, graded by locked tests, with an LLM-vs-deterministic-policy head-to-head. See docs/agentic-tasks-roadmap.md.
question: Which modeling tasks genuinely require an LLM agent — where a deterministic policy has no move for the real fix — and can the agent build a passing process-bigraph model for them?
hypothesis: As task complexity moves from calibration → regulatory coupling → simulator selection + subcellular composition, the deterministic policy fails while an LLM agent reasons the fix.

studies.name: bounded-cell
studies.title: Bounded goal-directed cell
studies.question: Build a bounded, goal-directed cell: on a finite nutrient pool and a rising temperature, produce a cell whose BIOMASS grows on the nutrient it CONSUMES (mass-conserving, Monod-saturating GROWTH), and whose VIABILITY holds while below its temperature tolerance then collapses once temperature exceeds it.

findings.statement: The cell grows its biomass on the nutrient it consumes, with Monod-saturating uptake feeding a yield-based growth step (MonodUptake + YieldGrowth). Growth rises with available nutrient but saturates rather than growing without bound, matching the intended Monod-limited phenotype. This confirms a bounded, goal-directed growth response driven by what the cell actually takes up.

evidence.observed: biomass grows on consumed nutrient via MonodUptake + YieldGrowth; behavior test 'growth' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: Growth is mass-conserving: the nutrient the cell consumes is accounted for as biomass gained rather than created or destroyed, and the finite nutrient pool is depleted as biomass accumulates. The MonodUptake and YieldGrowth processes are wired over the shared biomass/nutrient/uptake_flux stores so uptake and growth stay balanced.

evidence.observed: consumed nutrient is conserved as biomass across the biomass/nutrient/uptake_flux stores; behavior test 'conservation' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: On a rising temperature ramp, viability holds while the cell is below its temperature tolerance and then collapses once temperature exceeds it. The ThermalDeath process with t_tol=43 degC produces this viability cliff, driven by the TemperatureRamp over the shared temperature and viability stores.

evidence.observed: viability holds below t_tol=43 degC then collapses once temperature exceeds it (ThermalDeath); behavior test 'viability-cliff' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: The cell grows its biomass on the nutrient it consumes, with Monod-saturating uptake feeding a yield-based growth step (MonodUptake + YieldGrowth). Growth rises with available nutrient but saturates rather than growing without bound, matching the intended Monod-limited phenotype. This confirms a bounded, goal-directed growth response driven by what the cell actually takes up.

studies.name: diauxie
studies.title: Diauxic growth (glucose→lactose)
studies.question: Build a cell that grows on a mixture of glucose and lactose with the DIAUXIC phenotype: it consumes glucose first, and only once glucose is exhausted does it switch to lactose — a sequential shift, not simultaneous co-consumption.

findings.statement: The cell exhibits the diauxic phenotype: it consumes glucose first and only switches to lactose once glucose is exhausted, a sequential shift rather than simultaneous co-consumption. CataboliteRepression — a Hill switch driven by glucose — gates LactoseUptake through a lac_repression store, and this repression coupling is what enforces the ordering.

evidence.observed: glucose is used up before lactose, enforced by CataboliteRepression gating LactoseUptake via lac_repression; behavior test 'diauxic-order' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The cell grows on both substrates: biomass accumulates from glucose during the first phase and from lactose after the switch, so neither fuel is left unused. GlucoseUptake and LactoseUptake both feed biomass over the shared glucose/lactose/biomass stores.

evidence.observed: biomass grows on both glucose and lactose across the two phases; behavior test 'growth' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: Lactose is consumed, but only in the second phase: while glucose remains, the lac_repression store holds LactoseUptake off, and lactose is drawn down only after glucose is exhausted and catabolite repression lifts. This confirms lactose utilization is gated rather than concurrent.

evidence.observed: lactose is drawn down only after glucose is exhausted and lac_repression lifts; behavior test 'lactose-consumed' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: The cell exhibits the diauxic phenotype: it consumes glucose first and only switches to lactose once glucose is exhausted, a sequential shift rather than simultaneous co-consumption. CataboliteRepression — a Hill switch driven by glucose — gates LactoseUptake through a lac_repression store, and this repression coupling is what enforces the ordering.

studies.name: multicellular
studies.title: Multicellular differentiation phenotype
studies.question: Produce a multicellular tissue with a spatial differentiation gradient: cells near a signalling niche stay stem, distal cells differentiate.

findings.statement: The phenotype requires a simulator that supports a lattice, diffusing fields, and cell fate together; the agent selected CPM (viva-cpm), which provides all three. This 'choose a simulator' move is exactly what the deterministic policy could not express, so it gave up.

evidence.observed: chosen CPM (viva-cpm) simulator supports lattice + fields + cell fate; behavior test 'simulator-fit' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The composite instantiates a multicellular tissue of at least four cells on the CPM lattice — a Wnt-secreting niche plus progenitor cells — rather than a single-cell model, giving the spatial substrate a differentiation gradient can form over.

evidence.observed: a multicellular tissue (>=4 cells) on the CPM lattice; behavior test 'multicellular' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: A diffusing Wnt field emanates from the secreting niche, and a StemnessFate subcell in each cell reads its local Wnt level to set fate: cells near the niche stay STEM while distal cells become DIFFERENTIATED, producing the spatial differentiation gradient the task requires.

evidence.observed: near STEM, far DIFFERENTIATED spatial gradient produced by the CPM composite; behavior test 'differentiation-gradient' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: The phenotype requires a simulator that supports a lattice, diffusing fields, and cell fate together; the agent selected CPM (viva-cpm), which provides all three. This 'choose a simulator' move is exactly what the deterministic policy could not express, so it gave up.

studies.name: sbml
studies.title: SBML model → COPASI → quality
studies.question: Build an SBML kinetic model of a linear metabolic pathway A→B→C that COPASI can load and simulate to a valid steady state, with total mass conserved and the terminal product C accumulating as the dominant species.

findings.statement: The agent-authored SBML kinetic model (libsbml) of the A->B->C pathway loads and simulates in the REAL COPASI backend (basico, via viva-copasi). Every verdict — validity, load, steady state, conservation, terminal product — is read from an actual COPASI simulation, not a mock; the deterministic policy gave up at 0/5 because authoring an SBML network is not an install.

evidence.observed: SBML model loaded + simulated in the real COPASI (basico) backend; behavior test 'copasi-loads' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The linear metabolic pathway A->B->C, built from mass-action reactions, runs to a valid steady state in COPASI with total mass conserved — the closed mass-action network neither creates nor loses material over the simulation.

evidence.observed: total mass conserved across the A->B->C pathway at steady state; behavior test 'mass-conserved' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The terminal product C accumulates as the dominant species. The agent recognised after building A->B that the pathway stopped at B and added the B->C reaction, so material flows through to the terminus rather than pooling at the intermediate.

evidence.observed: terminal product C accumulates as the dominant species; behavior test 'terminal-product' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: The agent-authored SBML kinetic model (libsbml) of the A->B->C pathway loads and simulates in the REAL COPASI backend (basico, via viva-copasi). Every verdict — validity, load, steady state, conservation, terminal product — is read from an actual COPASI simulation, not a mock; the deterministic policy gave up at 0/5 because authoring an SBML network is not an install.

studies.name: multiscale
studies.title: Multiscale coupling via a translator
studies.question: Couple a cell-scale metabolic model (which produces a metabolite FLUX) to a tissue-scale spatial DIFFUSION FIELD of that metabolite, so that the cell's secretion sources the field and a gradient forms around the cell — with mass conserved across the scale interface.

findings.statement: The cell-scale CellMetabolism process is active as a metabolite source, secreting a flux in mol/time. This is the upstream half of the two-scale coupling — the cell whose secretion must source the tissue field.

evidence.observed: CellMetabolism secretes a metabolite flux (mol/time); behavior test 'cell-active' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: An agent-authored FluxTranslator maps the cell's secreted flux onto the DiffusionField's per-grid source, so the cell's secretion sources the 1-D concentration field (mM) and a diffusion gradient forms around the cell across the scale interface. The deterministic policy gave up at 1/4 because 'author a translator' is not an install it can express.

evidence.observed: cell secretion sources the 1-D diffusion field and a gradient forms around the cell; behavior test 'coupled-gradient' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The FluxTranslator carries the unit conversion (mol/time -> mM/time over the compartment volume, i.e. divide by volume) that conserves total mass across the cell-to-tissue scale interface, so no mass is created or lost when the cell's flux becomes the field's source.

evidence.observed: unit conversion (divide by volume) conserves mass across the scale interface; behavior test 'flux-conserved' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: The cell-scale CellMetabolism process is active as a metabolite source, secreting a flux in mol/time. This is the upstream half of the two-scale coupling — the cell whose secretion must source the tissue field.

studies.name: diagnosis
studies.title: Ambiguous diagnosis (why is biomass low?)
studies.question: A cell's biomass is far below target. Diagnose the cause from the observables and add the mechanism that fixes it, so the cell both grows (biomass >= 3.0) and stays alive (viability >= 0.5).

findings.statement: Low biomass was caused by the cell DYING, not by a broken yield or uptake pathway — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, so uptake is fine; viability crashed, so the cell is dying). Adding the correct mechanism, stabilize_membrane against the MembraneStress viability decay, restores growth so biomass reaches its target (biomass >= 3.0).

evidence.observed: stabilize_membrane fix lifts biomass to the >= 3.0 target once the dying-cell cause is diagnosed; behavior test 'growth' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: CellGrowth is gated by viability, so keeping the cell alive is what enables growth. The stabilize_membrane fix arrests the MembraneStress viability decay and holds viability above its survival threshold (viability >= 0.5), which is the precondition the joint observable panel identified for recovery.

evidence.observed: stabilize_membrane holds viability >= 0.5 by arresting MembraneStress decay; behavior test 'survives' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: Low biomass was caused by the cell DYING, not by a broken yield or uptake pathway — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, so uptake is fine; viability crashed, so the cell is dying). Adding the correct mechanism, stabilize_membrane against the MembraneStress viability decay, restores growth so biomass reaches its target (biomass >= 3.0).

studies.name: bistable
studies.title: Bistable genetic switch
studies.question: Build a bistable genetic switch: two mutually repressing genes A and B that settle into two DISTINCT stable states and latch to whichever gene starts ahead (a decisive toggle, not a graded midpoint).

findings.statement: Cooperative (Hill n=2) mutual repression between two genes A and B destabilises the symmetric fixed point and opens two distinct stable basins, so the composite settles into one of two decisive states rather than a graded midpoint. Confirmed: the agent-built ToggleSwitch reaches a state separation of 3.46 between the two basins, where the deterministic policy — which only tuned expression strength, a knob — stayed monostable at separation 0.

evidence.observed: state separation 3.46 between the two settled states (vs 0 for the monostable expression-tuning policy); behavior test 'bistable' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The switch latches to whichever gene starts ahead, resolving to a single dominant gene rather than relaxing to a symmetric midpoint — the decisive toggle the task requires. The same cooperative feedback makes this self-reinforcing: once one basin is entered it is held.

evidence.observed: the composite resolves to one dominant gene with no graded midpoint; behavior test 'decisive' == within_tol, gate passed

derived.insight: Cooperative (Hill n=2) mutual repression between two genes A and B destabilises the symmetric fixed point and opens two distinct stable basins, so the composite settles into one of two decisive states rather than a graded midpoint. Confirmed: the agent-built ToggleSwitch reaches a state separation of 3.46 between the two basins, where the deterministic policy — which only tuned expression strength, a knob — stayed monostable at separation 0.
